limitations: This was a closed, read-only replay. No provider/model call, protected test access, release action, fresh rebuild, or test execution was performed by the auditor; dynamic R2 claims were evaluated from manifest-bound retained captures plus independent byte/path/hash replay.

Absence of result access before BFCL preregistration was assessed solely from the closed evidence, timestamps, absent result artifacts, and fail-closed validation code; no external history was queried.

findings.rationale: The importer accepts two caller-supplied mode-0700 attempt directories whose process metadata, thread IDs, events, output, and hashes are all locally self-authored. Neither the importer nor authorization replay verifies a trusted issuer signature or protected provider attestation. A caller can synthesize two distinct thread.started IDs and matching PASS outputs, after which the fixed importer mints accepted R0-R2 receipts and the bootstrap aggregate. The tests themselves construct synthetic AI runs which pass the raw-run validator.
findings.required_action: Require cryptographically authenticated issuer/provider provenance over the process metadata, event stream, output, bundle identity, model, reasoning effort, and provider thread identity, or import exclusively from an equivalently protected attested channel. Add a negative test proving two syntactically valid locally fabricated attempts cannot mint the aggregate.
findings.title: R0-R2 AI attempts remain unauthenticated

findings.rationale: Non-bootstrap completion sites require an accepted R3 ledger entry, but R3 acceptance itself has no fixed trusted importer. The generic ledger API accepts a locally created AI_INDEPENDENT stage receipt after locally created AUTHOR_CANDIDATE and REVIEW_REQUIRED entries. Authorization then accepts that self-declared R3 receipt and the post-R3 provider gate trusts the resulting ledger state.
findings.required_action: Create a fixed R3 review importer with authenticated independent-review provenance, bind the active R3 ledger transition exclusively to its output, and reject generic or caller-selected accepted R3 receipts at authorization.
findings.title: The R3 prerequisite is caller-mintable

findings.rationale: The fixed-input, one-use test capability and topology bindings exist, but the required independent approval is derived from unauthenticated caller-supplied AI attempt directories. Consequently the approval artifact is not trustworthy even though its downstream consumption is atomic.
findings.required_action: Authenticate both AI primary attempts with trusted issuer/provider attestations before importing the one-full-test approval, while preserving the existing exact-input and one-use consumption bindings.
findings.title: Full-test approval lacks trusted independent provenance

findings.rationale: The dedicated importer replays hashes and raw event syntax but does not establish that Codex or another trusted issuer produced them. All accepted provenance fields, including two distinct provider thread IDs, can be written by the caller before import, allowing a forged APPROVE_ONE_FULL_TEST artifact.
findings.required_action: Add non-forgeable issuer/provider authentication to the test-access attempt format and verify it in both the importer and consuming gate. Include adversarial locally fabricated-attempt tests.
findings.title: The test-access importer accepts forged AI provenance

findings.rationale: Completion transports are routed through either the fixed bootstrap adapter or the post-R3 gate, but the latter derives authority from a generic, self-authenticating R3 receipt. Thus a caller can manufacture accepted R3 state and unlock arbitrary post-R3 planned call counts without a genuine R3 review.
findings.required_action: Make accepted R3 authority artifact-derived from a fixed authenticated importer and prohibit the generic stage-ledger API from creating an authorization-eligible R3 acceptance. Test the complete forged AUTHOR/REVIEW/ACCEPTED sequence before network I/O.
findings.title: The post-R3 completion boundary trusts forgeable R3 state

findings.rationale: The importer CLI registers --attempt-ledger twice on the same ArgumentParser. Argparse raises a conflicting-option error while constructing the parser, so the documented fixed test-access importer entry point cannot run.
findings.required_action: Remove the duplicate option registration and add an end-to-end CLI parser/import smoke test.
findings.title: The full-test approval importer CLI cannot start

findings.rationale: After a successful post-R3 preflight writes AUTHORIZED_READY_FOR_POST_R3_EXECUTION, main compares the status only with AUTHORIZED_READY_FOR_T2_EXECUTION and exits 3. This produces a contradictory successful authorization artifact and failing process result.
findings.required_action: Use phase-specific success statuses and add a CLI test asserting a successful post-R3 preflight exits zero without changing the fail-closed authorization checks.
findings.title: Successful post-R3 preflight always exits as failure

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Bootstrap authorization requires the fixed importer aggregate and active identity receipt, while release entry points are unconditionally disabled; caller-supplied success mappings cannot directly authorize either boundary.
The expressly required trusted issuer cryptographic signature is absent; self-authored raw attempts can mint importer output.
The importer emits accepted receipts only for an all-accepted, zero-P0/P1, exact-bootstrap disposition; a REVISE response is rejected without minting acceptance.
Claim validation binds candidate.4, the active inventory root, exact gate sets, distinct receipt files, strict gate semantics, and AI-independent acceptance.
The ledger uses immutable hash-chained snapshots, atomic pre-I/O claims, native acceptance and terminal accounting, strict transitions, and incomplete-history failure semantics.

The 428-file source inventory, 387-entry executed closure, retained rebuild/fresh-install captures, all 65 wheel payload/source pairs including package data, and all 192 upstream BFCL tracked files replay exactly.
The transport checks R3 state, but authorization-eligible accepted R3 state can be created through the generic ledger from a self-authored receipt.
Case/topology/input and one-use bindings exist, but the AI replacement approval lacks authenticated independent provenance.

The final preregistration freezes 216 unique cases, exact 80/122/24 categories, languages, coherent worker/adapter/ledger/dependency identities, and validates per-step ledger receipts after the freeze.

Serving gates rebuild cells from fixed raw receipts and the active ledger, enforcing workload identity, exact ledger coverage, globally unique native IDs, and non-overlapping windows; active zero digests keep the future gate closed.
The audit schema truthfully fixes AI authority, PRIMARY role, closed boundaries, no human claim, and no direct model/test/release authorization.
The materialized six-row ledger is the single reconciled append-only R0-R2 source, with contiguous sequence, hash chain, supersession links, active source identity, and checkpoint prefix replay.

Standalone caller-selected R0-R2 receipts are rejected; authorization requires the fixed aggregate and replays both raw-event-bound xhigh run receipts. The remaining origin-authentication defect is tracked under DG10-C3-AI-002.
The dedicated importer exists but its raw provider provenance is locally forgeable and therefore not independent.
Exactly 24 deterministic slots are preallocated, one fixed ledger/latch/capability is used, each slot is atomically claimed once, and the sealed adapter permits one provider request per slot.
runtime/migrations/script.py.mako is materialized, inventoried, included in the executed closure, and byte-equal to the corresponding wheel member.
The immutable successor contract and runner consistently require gpt-5.6-sol with xhigh; interrupted max attempts have no acceptance effect.
The independently rebuilt wheel bytes are retained and hash-identical to the source wheel at 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773.
The sole full-test executor atomically consumes the fixed approval before protected access, binds exact inputs, rejects reuse, and revalidates afterward.
Collection and pytest explicitly use -c evals/dg10/pyproject.toml --rootdir ., Ruff explicitly uses --config, and the config digest is closure-bound.
Each fixed slot receives a durable exclusive provider claim before network open, and repeat/direct/concurrent claims fail before I/O.

BFCL worker closure, execution identity, case manifest, and stage records have ordered aware timestamps; the stage entries follow the effective amendment, and scoring requires result access strictly after manifest freeze.
The active R1 validation embeds the complete 428-entry inventory with root a9a7c8ee785c6fd77fb8e064ee25c2e8541da411b9ee03a39a860b29d8b2d50f, and ledger replay checks its internal identity.
All known completion sites use a nominal boundary, but the post-R3 branch trusts a generic self-authored accepted R3 receipt, so it is not artifact-derived or non-bypassable.

DG10-R0.rationale: All 201 materialized candidate.2 members replay to the recorded paths, sizes, and hashes; the archive receipt and control-file hashes agree; all SHA256SUMS entries pass; and both final-audit copies preserve the immutable NO_GO_RELEASE_STOPPED decision with model, full-test, and release authority false. The complete 001-024 register and successor chain are materialized without erasing history.

DG10-R1.rationale: Claim binding, append-only call accounting, exact 24-slot bootstrap execution, atomic test consumption, truthful AI authority, serving replay, and release denial are substantially fail-closed. R1 nevertheless fails because R0-R2 and test-access importers trust locally forgeable AI provenance, and generic self-authored accepted R3 receipts can unlock non-bootstrap model authorization. Two additional CLI contradictions are material P2 defects.

Fresh-install captures bind Python 3.11.13, uv.lock, 51 installed distributions, import probe, 254 collected and passed tests, and explicit pytest/Ruff configuration.
